summary: Curry County, OR lookout site: platform c.1918, shake cabin 1924, L-4 cab 1932; staffed into the 1940s and removed or destroyed in 1965; no current site report.

facts.design: L-4 cab (1932), after a 1924 shake cabin and a c.1918 10-foot platform
facts.status_note: The L-4 cab was removed or destroyed in 1965; no source describes what remains

events.note: Newspaper item (Siskiyou Bulletin) says Charles Simons erected a sort of tower at his lookout. Conflicts with the c.1918 platform date in the register and firelookout.com.
Charles Simons at Bear Camp, described as the lookout (Siskiyou Bulletin, August 1914)
Material for the Bear Camp lookout cabin on the ground; to be built on the California Bulletin plan (Siskiyou Bulletin). Not clearly the 1924 shake cabin.
Charles Simons back at Bear Camp after military training (Siskiyou Bulletin)
Bear Camp received one of four fire finders issued to lookouts in the county (Grants Pass Daily Courier, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Cabin found broken into in June; most equipment moved out or knocked down (Siskiyou Bulletin)
J.P. Emery worked every summer since 1927 as lookout-fireman and lookout (Siskiyou Bulletin, 1932)
Emery found and put out two small fires near his station (Siskiyou Bulletin, September 1932)
L-4 cab replaced the shake cabin in 1932 (register; firelookout.com). Forest Lookouts describes the 1932 house as an Aladdin style lookout house.
Lookout Lawson Thomas reported smoke to Rand Ranger Station; a 15-man crew was on its way to the fire by 7:35 a.m. (Forest Lookouts, August 1933)
Station staffed 100 days; reported to the Rand Ranger Station by forest telephone line
Aircraft Warning Service station 'George 8-2' activated June 10 and deactivated October 16, 1943 (Forest Lookouts)
L-4 cab removed in 1965 (register); firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1914 newspaper item says a tower was erected at the lookout; the register and firelookout.com date a 10-foot platform to about 1918. The sources do not reconcile the two dates, so the story gives both.
A 1915 item describes a cabin being built on the California Bulletin plan; the register and firelookout.com date the shake cabin to 1924. The sources do not say whether these are the same building.
The register and firelookout.com call the 1932 building an L-4 cab; Forest Lookouts calls it an Aladdin style lookout house. Reported as both.
The register says the L-4 cab was removed in 1965; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965. Both give 1965, so the story reports the year and both verbs.

notes_for_editor: Three sources read; the Forest Lookouts page is a compilation of dated newspaper and Forest Service items, and only items about the lookout are used. Not used: firelookout.com heading 'R.I.P. 1924-1932' conflicts with its own text (L-4 cab 1932 to 1965). Lead for a future pass: a Siskiyou National Forest lookout inventory PDF (digital.sou.edu, collection p16085coll18, id 41128) lists Bear Camp with 1932 and 1965 dates in its appendix table; the table layout did not extract cleanly, so it is not cited. The 1915 cabin's relation to the 1924 shake cabin is unresolved. No new photos found.
